cues.zh: 所以，

cues.zh: 并不是说菜单和工具栏

cues.zh: 不是个好的

cues.zh: 最早关于菜单的规范，同样出自 Xerox，说菜单上的项目不应超过七个。可当你有一个像 Office 这样功能繁多的程序时，

cues.zh: 总有一天，空间会不够用。所以我们需要打造一套新的用户界面。

cues.en: And we also thought that this was an opportunity to do what we called reawakening the soul of the software. It was an opportunity to redefine
cues.zh: 我们也觉得，这是个机会，可以做我们所说的“唤醒软件的灵魂”。这是个重新定义的机会，

cues.zh: 重新定义 Word、Excel 和 PowerPoint 的意义。

cues.en: It was a new it was a chance to rethink the applications,
cues.zh: 这是一次重新思考这些应用的机会，

cues.en: knowing with the with with hindsight how they turned out, what features had we added over time.
cues.zh: 回头看它们最终的样子，以及这些年来我们陆续添加了哪些功能。

cues.en: And so with that I'm gonna do a quick literally two minute demo of Office '2 thousand and seven
cues.zh: 那么接下来，我花大概两分钟快速演示一下 Office 2007，

cues.en: to show you a couple of concepts and just in case anyone in here hasn't seen it before. So this is a Word document here, this is a new user interface, and I just have some text that I dumped into here.
cues.zh: 展示几个核心概念，也照顾一下还没见过的朋友。这里是一个 Word 文档，采用了全新的用户界面，我先随便放了些文本进去。

cues.zh: 我打算做一份关于澳大利亚的宣传册。

cues.en: And so the first thing to note is the ribbon, is the area at the top, which is the tabbed set of commands. And the Home tab is designed to be very familiar to people who've used the standard and formatting toolbars in Office before. So it's pretty simple to grab some text,
cues.zh: 首先映入眼帘的是功能区（Ribbon），也就是顶部这块带标签页的命令区。对于熟悉旧版 Office “常用”和“格式”工具栏的人来说，“开始”标签页上手会非常自然。所以操作很简单，比如选中一段文本，

cues.en: click center,
cues.zh: 点击居中，

cues.en: and it works very similar to the standard toolbar. We also have something throughout the UI which is called Live Preview.
cues.zh: 效果和以前的标准工具栏基本一致。此外，我们在整个 UI 中加入了一个叫“实时预览”（Live Preview）的功能。

cues.en: Which says that any time you hover over
cues.zh: 就是说，只要你把鼠标悬停在

cues.en: a formatting choice, we'll show you exactly what it looks like. You don't have to do a lot of trial and error, a lot of click undo, click undo, click undo.
cues.zh: 某个格式选项上，我们就会确切地展示出它是什么效果。你不用反复试错，不用一直点撤销、点撤销、点撤销。

cues.zh: 在这里，因为这是我宣传册的标题，我可能更想用一个样式。这里我就用标题样式。同样可以看到，这些也都有实时预览。我们把它叫做标题。

cues.en: And now I'm going to insert a picture.
cues.zh: 现在我要插入一张图片。

cues.en: So I click insert,
cues.zh: 所以我点“插入”，

cues.en: picture,
cues.zh: “图片”，

cues.en: choose this cute koala.
cues.zh: 选这只可爱的考拉。

cues.en: And as you can see this picture inserted itself like pictures always do in Word and how you hardly ever want them to, which is with the text sort of displacing the text and with the text starting down here.
cues.zh: 你们可以看到，这张图片插进来了。在 Word 里，图片总是这样插入，而这往往不是你想要的效果：文字被挤开，只能从下面这里开始。

cues.en: So what I'm gonna do is use the position gallery.
cues.zh: 所以我要用“位置”图库。

cues.en: Which again just shows you the most common places that people want to put pictures
cues.zh: 它会显示大家最常把图片放在文档中的哪些位置，

cues.en: in their documents and shows you with live preview where it's gonna end up. So as I click this one, you'll see that word scrolls in into view to show me the picture. And I wanna give this a cool effect. So these visual things that I've popped down are called galleries.
cues.zh: 还会通过实时预览告诉你图片最终会出现在哪里。点这个选项时，你会看到 Word 滚动到相应位置，让我看到图片。我还想给它加个酷炫的效果。我刚才展开的这些视觉选项叫作图库。

cues.en: And galleries are the way of showing the results of the feature as opposed to the commands themselves. And they're designed to be very visual, so you can see as I hover over different effects here, I can make it look like
cues.zh: 样式库不是直接展示命令本身，而是用来呈现该功能最终效果的。它们被设计得非常直观，大家可以看到，当我悬停在不同的效果上时，可以让它看起来像

cues.en: a picture, I can tilt it, or I can give it a reflection
cues.zh: 一张照片，可以倾斜它，或者给它加个倒影，

cues.en: until I find one that looks like what I want to. This This case I'm gonna give it this very simple
cues.zh: 直到找到我满意的效果为止。这次我打算给它加上这个非常简单的

cues.en: white frame here.
cues.zh: 白色边框。

cues.zh: 现在我想把它排版得更像一本宣传册。

cues.en: So the first thing that I'm gonna do here is change the orientation of the page to landscape, again using a gallery, just choose orientation landscape.
cues.zh: 首先我要做的是把页面方向改成横向，同样用功能区，选方向里的横向。

cues.en: I'm gonna use my live zoom at the bottom to zoom this out to the point where I can see the whole page so that I can sort of get a sense of it a little bit better. I'll split the text into columns, I'll just choose columns,
cues.zh: 我用底部的实时缩放把页面缩小到能看见整页，这样能更好地感受一下整体效果。然后我把文本分栏，直接选分栏，

cues.zh: 我们做的一件

cues.en: cool things that we've done is even things like margins that used to take going into a dialog box. You can now set the most common margins or the ones that you've used recently. Again, just using a very visual
cues.zh: 很酷的事情是，像以前必须在对话框里设置的页边距，现在也能直接选最常用的或最近用过的了。同样也是通过非常直观的

cues.en: thing.
cues.zh: 视觉方式来实现。

cues.zh: 我们希望实现的另一种工作方式，是把整个界面空间都还给你的文档。而且因为所有的

cues.en: commands from Office are put into the ribbon, like there's no additional toolbars and other junk, it's also very easy to get rid of it. So I can right click and choose minimize the ribbon. And now the entire UI has turned into just one little strip at the top. cues.zh: Office 命令都收录到了功能区（Ribbon）中，没有任何多余的工具栏和其他杂项，所以隐藏起来也特别方便。我只需右键点击，选择“最小化功能区”。现在整个 UI 就缩减成了顶部的一条细栏。你仍然能以类似弹出的方式使用功能区，但用完它就会自动隐藏，为你腾出更多空间来查看文档。以这种方式工作时，

cues.en: one of the cool things that you can do
cues.zh: 有一个很酷的功能

cues.en: is called the mini toolbar. So I'm gonna select some text and if you look just above the cursor, you'll see a little faded in toolbar that has the most common formatting commands
cues.zh: 叫作迷你工具栏。我现在选定一段文字，大家看光标正上方，会看到一个半透明浮现的工具栏，里面包含了最常用的格式化命令

cues.en: right above it. As I move my mouse to it, you'll see that it fades in. If I move my mouse anywhere other than towards it, you'll see that it's very shy, it just totally goes away. But if I move towards it, I can see the most commonly used formatting commands. So if I want to shrink this down a little bit to make it fit,
cues.zh: 就在它上方。当我把鼠标移过去时，它就会完全显现。如果我把鼠标移开，它就很“害羞”，直接完全消失了。但如果我移向它，就能看到最常用的格式化命令。所以如果我想稍微把它缩小一点以适合版面，

cues.zh: 直接操作就行，甚至完全不需要用到功能区（Ribbon）。

cues.zh: 不过今天，

cues.zh: 我可以加页码

cues.zh: 非常简单，就选页码，放在页面底部，挑个好看的样式。我还没想好要哪种，这个挺酷的。

cues.en: So I get a sort of bracketed number at the bottom. And the final thing I'll do here is just add a quick cover page.
cues.zh: 这样底部就有了带括号的页码。最后我要做的就是快速加个封面页。

cues.en: This looks sorta cool. Although this train doesn't really make a whole lot of sense for Australia. So I think what I'll do is just choose Change Picture
cues.zh: 这看起来还挺酷的。不过这列火车对澳大利亚来说不太合适。我想我就点“更改图片”吧

cues.en: and choose a nice little picture there and I'm done. So that sort of gives you a quick overview of how I took some just plain text and turned it into something really cool in just a few seconds, all visually. I didn't use really commands, I just used sort of galleries and live preview to make this thing look cool.
cues.zh: 再选一张好看的小图片，就搞定了。这大概就是个快速演示：我怎么把纯文本变成很酷的东西，只用了几秒钟，而且全程都是可视化操作。我没怎么用命令，只是用了一些图库和实时预览，让它看起来更酷。

cues.en: So that's the Office user interface.
cues.zh: 这就是 Office 的用户界面。

cues.en: And there's a lot more that I didn't show you. It's really not just the ribbon. I called this the story of the ribbon, but it's more than that. Because there's a whole lot of things that work together to make the user interface work.
cues.zh: 我没展示出来的还有很多。它真的不只是功能区（Ribbon）。虽然我把这称为 Ribbon 的故事，但内容远不止于此。因为整个界面的顺畅运作，背后有非常多的机制在协同配合。

cues.en: But really the key concept behind it is this thing called results oriented design,
cues.zh: 但其背后的核心理念，其实是所谓的“以结果为导向的设计”，

cues.en: which is mean as opposed to thinking about commands
cues.zh: 它的意思是不是去关注指令，

cues.en: like execute this command, execute this command, execute this command, we try to think about functionality
cues.zh: 比如执行这个命令、执行那个命令，而是尝试去思考功能本身，

cues.en: that we could put together discreetly
cues.zh: 将这些功能精简地整合在一起，

cues.en: and present at a higher level.
cues.zh: 并在更高维度上呈现给用户。

cues.en: And then figure out how to display it visually.
cues.zh: 然后再想办法把它可视化地展示出来。

cues.en: So instead of showing a bunch of commands, show the picture of what it's gonna look like. And make it sort of fun to play with it.
cues.zh: 所以与其展示一堆命令，不如直接展示它最终会是什么样子。还要让它玩起来有点意思。

cues.en: And so people would try different things out, and that would help them learn about the product.
cues.zh: 这样人们就会尝试不同的东西，这能帮他们了解这个产品。

cues.en: So this is the design process that we used. And there's sort of four steps to it.
cues.zh: 这就是我们采用的设计流程。大致有四个步骤。

cues.en: Research,
cues.zh: 调研，

cues.en: the formulation of design tenets,
cues.zh: 提炼设计原则，

cues.en: prototypes,
cues.zh: 做原型，

cues.en: and evaluation.
cues.zh: 以及评估。

cues.en: The first one I'm gonna talk about is the research that went into it.
cues.zh: 我要讲的第一部分，是这项研究的来龙去脉。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: whenever I talk about interface design to people at Microsoft,
cues.zh: 每次我和微软的人聊界面设计时，

cues.en: I always talk about it being one part art and one part science.
cues.zh: 我总会说，界面设计一半是艺术，一半是科学。

cues.en: There's no book that you can read that can teach you exactly how to do it because part of it is art, and you need to understand the art part and the science part.
cues.zh: 没有哪本书能教会你具体该怎么做，因为其中一部分是艺术。你得理解艺术的那一面，也得理解科学的那一面。

cues.en: Art is all about
cues.zh: 对我来说，艺术关乎

cues.en: language for me. User interface is really the language that software uses
cues.zh: 语言。用户界面其实就是软件用来与你交流的语言，

cues.en: to communicate to you what's what's possible. It's the sort of medium between the the computer and the human.
cues.zh: 它告诉你有哪些可能。它是计算机与人之间的一种媒介。

cues.en: Now people have an amazingly emotional experience
cues.zh: 现在人与计算机之间的关系，

cues.en: with a relationship with their computer. Anyone who's ever like slammed a mouse down or
cues.zh: 有着极其丰富的情感体验。任何曾经摔过鼠标、

cues.en: slammed their keyboard down or occasionally see pictures of people who threw their monitor on the ground, that's emotional. cues.zh: 砸过键盘，或者偶尔看到有人把显示器摔在地上的人，都能体会到那种情绪。实际上几年前有项研究表明，Office 用户花在 Word 和 Excel 上的单处时间，比陪配偶的时间还要多。

cues.zh: 但这也说明这种情感关系

cues.zh: 很重要。这是你每天要花很多时间打交道的东西。

cues.zh: 所以我们想看看人们在自然环境中、在工作场所、在家里对 Office 的反应。

cues.zh: 我们最终收集了一万小时的用户使用 Office 的视频，

cues.en: people ranting to us, reality
cues.zh: 人们对着我们吐槽，真人

cues.zh: 秀节目式的，人们走到镜头前向我们倾诉。我们想知道的是，人们使用 Office 时是什么感受。

cues.en: We felt like if we solve these four goals that we would have a successful UI redesign.

cues.en: And so we had to come up with the design tenets that we felt like if we followed them, would lead us to that mountain. Right? This was the mountain. The design tenets were the path to take to get there. And here were the design tenets that we came up with.
cues.zh: 因此我们必须确立几条设计原则，相信只要遵循它们，就能登上那座山峰，对吧？目标就是山峰，而设计原则就是通往那里的路径。这就是我们最终定下的设计原则。

cues.en: A person's focus should be on the content, not on the UI.
cues.zh: 人的注意力应放在内容上，而不是界面上。

cues.en: Help people work without interference.
cues.zh: 帮助人们不受干扰地工作。

cues.en: Interference for us was clippy popping up, toolbars popping up, just junk popping up everywhere. Help people work without interference.
cues.zh: 对我们来说，干扰就是 Clippy 弹出来、工具栏弹出来，到处都是乱七八糟的东西。帮助人们不受干扰地工作。

cues.en: Reduce the number of choices presented at any given time. This is about contextualization.
cues.zh: 减少任何时候呈现的选项数量。这关乎情境化。

cues.en: When there's 1,500 companions in Office, it's impossible to have them all memorized. So you have to find a way of only showing the table tools when you actually have a table up. Otherwise, you'll get swamped. Increase efficiency.
cues.zh: 当 Office 里有 1500 个助手时，不可能把它们全记住。所以你得想办法只在真正打开表格时才显示表格工具。否则你会被淹没。提高效率。

cues.en: We know that that if you can improve people's efficiency,
cues.zh: 我们知道，如果你能提升人们的效率，

cues.en: they'll react positively.
cues.zh: 他们就会积极响应。

cues.en: Consistency over homogeneity.
cues.zh: 一致性胜过同质化。

cues.en: Having consistency between word and excel is good, but if you don't let excel be excel and word be word, then they're gonna feel unnatural. This was about bringing out the soul of the software.
cues.zh: Word 和 Excel 保持一致是好事，但如果不让 Excel 像 Excel、Word 像 Word，用起来就会显得不自然。这是在展现软件的灵魂。

cues.en: Giving features a permanent home.
cues.zh: 为功能提供固定的位置。

cues.en: So this was about, there's one place to go find a command, as opposed to smart UI, like IntelliJunk that would sort of move the command stuff around for you. This is like there's just a straightforward place for it to be.
cues.zh: 也就是说，找命令时有一个固定的地方可去，而不是像 IntelliJunk 那种智能界面，擅自挪动命令的位置。这里就是让命令有个简单明了的固定位置。

cues.en: And finally, straightforward is better than clever. This is a reminder to ourselves not to over design.
cues.zh: 最后一条，直白胜过耍小聪明。这是在提醒我们自己不要过度设计。

cues.en: That every time we come up with a clever, super optimized solution,
cues.zh: 每当我们想出一个看似巧妙、极度优化的方案时，

cues.en: that it would be better to go back to the straightforward thing, because no one would understand
cues.zh: 最好还是回归直白简单的做法，因为除了我们自己，

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 根本

cues.en: super clever thing except for us. And so this is how we use design tenets again and again. So someone has a design idea. Like hey, wouldn't it be cool if Clippy came up and looked like you're writing a letter? Well, we take that idea and we validate it against the tenants. We say, well, one of our tenants is straightforward is better than clever. This seems like an awful, clever thing.
cues.zh: 没人能看懂那个自作聪明的玩意儿。这就是我们反复践行设计原则的方式。比如有人提出了一个设计想法：“嘿，要是让 Clippy 跳出来，显示你好像在写信，岂不是很酷？”那好，我们就会拿这个想法对照设计原则去检验。我们会说，我们有一条原则是“直白胜过耍小聪明”，而这个点子看起来完全是在抖机灵。

cues.en: And so we nix it. Right? We did this again and again and again in using the design tenants to help us make decisions.
cues.zh: 于是我们就把它砍掉，对吧？我们一次次地用设计原则来帮助自己做决策。

cues.en: The final thing I would say about these, our design tenants have to be religion.
cues.zh: 关于这些，我想说的最后一点是，我们的设计原则必须成为一种信仰。

cues.en: If everyone on your team doesn't know the design tenants, can't recite them,
cues.zh: 如果你团队里不是每个人都了解这些设计原则，背都背不出来，

cues.en: then people are gonna make bad decisions. And we presented them, we presented them humorously, we presented them seriously,
cues.zh: 那人们就会做出糟糕的决定。我们把这些原则展示出来，有时幽默地展示，有时严肃地展示，

cues.en: we filmed me on video in people's inboxes, reading them to them. We did everything we could to get people understanding the design tenets. So when the developer is sitting in his office at 3AM,
cues.zh: 我们把我的视频录下来发到大家的收件箱里，读给他们听。我们想尽一切办法让人理解这些设计原则。这样当开发者凌晨3点坐在办公室，

cues.en: making the code change, and there's no designer there to look over his shoulder, that he makes the right kind of decision. That's that's what design tenets are all about.
cues.zh: 改代码的时候，身边没有设计师盯着，他也能做出正确的决定。这就是设计原则的意义所在。

cues.en: And the reason for this is something called Fitt's Law.

cues.zh: 简化后的费茨定律

cues.en: basically
cues.zh: 基本上

cues.zh: 讲的是这样一个关系

cues.zh: 物体离鼠标光标有多近、有多大，

cues.zh: 与获取该目标有多容易之间的关系。所以一个离得远的大按钮容易点，一个离光标近的小按钮也容易点，

cues.en: and then as you move further away or get smaller, it gets harder. cues.zh: 而当你离得更远或者按钮变得更小时，就更难了。所以这里的想法是，如果我们能把一堆UI放在光标旁边，那么点击它就会非常非常容易，会非常简单。于是我们开始研究不同的方法，把UI放到光标周围，看看怎样才合理。当然，这就演变成了迷你工具栏。当时我们把它叫做floaty。

cues.zh: 也就是说，想象一下，我们为浮动 UI 腾出空间的方式是：它出现时，把其他内容推开。我们叫它「推开器」，就是把周围的东西挪开，给它腾出空间。

cues.zh: 所谓的长期可用性，是指对用户进行为期数月的跟踪测试。

cues.en: We found out that people's experience using,
cues.zh: 我们发现，用户在体验产品时，

cues.en: especially something like Office that they had some familiarity with, using it in the lab for the first two hours
cues.zh: 尤其是像 Office 这种他们本就有些熟悉的产品，让他在实验室里用上最初的两小时，

cues.en: doesn't tell you very much about how well your UI is working. Basically only tells you how well it works for these first two hours. You really needed to see how people
cues.zh: 根本看不出你的 UI 到底好不好用。基本上只能反映出头两个小时的效果。你其实需要观察用户

cues.en: reacted in week one, in week three, in month one, in month three. And that's what longitudinal usability
cues.zh: 在第一周、第三周，以及第一个月、第三个月的反应。这就是长期可用性测试

cues.en: gave us. People that used early builds of the product for months gave us our feedback, and we were able to make a ton of changes based on that.
cues.zh: 带给我们的价值。用户连续几个月使用产品的早期构建版本，并向我们反馈，我们也因此做出了大量的修改。

cues.en: So the single hardest thing that we had to do,
cues.zh: 所以我们要做的最难的一件事，

cues.en: I would say, in terms of evaluation, was evaluating feature organization.
cues.zh: 我想，从评估的角度来说，是评估功能的组织方式。

cues.en: Now there are a lot of commands in Office, as you've seen. And trying to figure out how to map all of the thousand or 1,500 commands into a new UI was a very daunting task, and it drove some people mad.
cues.zh: 你们也看到了，Office 里有很多命令。要想办法把一千到一千五百条命令映射到新的界面里，着实让人头疼，也把一些人逼疯了。

cues.en: The first idea we had was writing them all on index cards. This is before we knew there were 1,500 of them. And getting like a conference room and like sort of spreading them out, like which one sort of made sense.
cues.zh: 我们最初的想法是把所有命令都写在索引卡上。那时我们还不知道有一千五百条。然后找个会议室，把卡片摊开，看看怎么分类比较合理。

cues.en: And quickly we realized we didn't have a big enough room
cues.zh: 我们很快就意识到，微软园区里

cues.en: on Microsoft campus to do that. And so we had to find other ways. But it's a very tricky thing because
cues.zh: 根本没有足够大的房间来做这件事。所以我们必须另寻他法。但这事儿非常棘手，因为

cues.en: you can come up with something that works really well for one person and it doesn't work well for another person. And
cues.zh: 你做出的某个方案可能对一个人很好用，对另一个人却完全不行。

cues.en: so we spent so much time refining and refining and refining feature organization
cues.zh: 因此我们花了大量时间，反反复复地打磨功能组织架构，

cues.en: from the very beginning to the very end.
cues.zh: 从头到尾一直在优化。

cues.en: In fact, I was just sitting in my hotel room last night, my wife was sitting across from me using her laptop. She's like, where is freeze panes in Excel?
cues.zh: 其实昨晚在酒店房间里，我妻子就坐在我对面用笔记本电脑。她突然问我：Excel 里的“冻结窗格”在哪儿？

cues.en: I'm like, well, where do you think it is? It's on the view tab. She's like, why is it a view thing? Like, well, 93%
cues.zh: 我就说：“你觉得它在哪儿？”“在「视图」选项卡里。”她说：“为什么这算视图里的东西？”我说：“嗯，93%

cues.en: of users believe it should be on the view tab.
cues.zh: 的用户都觉得它应该放在「视图」选项卡里。”

cues.en: It's like, what doesn't belong on the view tab? Well, where do you think it should go? Well, I don't know, but not on the view tab.
cues.zh: 她又说：“什么东西不该放在「视图」选项卡里？”我问：“那你觉得应该放哪儿？”她说：“我不知道，但反正不该放在「视图」选项卡里。”

cues.en: So we have a lot of different ways of evaluating feature organization.
cues.zh: 所以，我们有很多不同的方法来评估功能的组织方式。

cues.en: We looked at things like feature affinity research,
cues.zh: 我们研究过功能亲和度，

cues.en: which is how do people use sets of things together. We do card sorts, and I'll show you the card sort thing that we use in a second. We look at command loops, which is if you have two commands that you use over and over again, and they're on different tabs,
cues.zh: 也就是人们如何搭配使用一组功能。我们会做卡片分类，等会儿我会给你们看我们用的卡片分类方法。我们还会看命令循环：如果你反复使用两个命令，而它们位于不同的选项卡上，

cues.en: every time it requires an extra click to switch tabs. Like use this one, switch tab, use this one. Switch tab, use this one. So you have to get the command loops eliminated.
cues.zh: 每次切换选项卡都得多点一下。比如用这个，切换选项卡，用那个；再切换选项卡，用这个。所以，得把这种命令循环消除掉。

cues.en: And the other tricky thing is you always have to get fresh eyes on the product. After you've used something for a couple of months, you're worthless because you already know how it works. And in fact, your beta users are worthless too because they're the same people who now know how it works. So you constantly have to get new people to look at stuff.
cues.zh: 另一个棘手的地方在于，你总得让没用过的人来看看产品。一旦你自己用了几个月，你的反馈就没价值了，因为你早就知道它是怎么运作的。事实上，你的测试用户也没参考价值了，因为他们也摸清了门道。所以你必须不断找新面孔来体验产品。

cues.en: One of the things we fought early on inside the organization
cues.zh: 我们早期在团队内部极力克服的一点，

cues.en: was the sense like the word team is like, but our commands are already ideally organized.
cues.zh: 就是有种类似“团队”的观念，觉得“我们的命令结构组织得已经很完美了”。

cues.en: Like they're already great, I don't understand why you would wanna reorganize them, everyone knows where they are. And so this was a slide that I showed them back in 2003.
cues.zh: 它们本来就很好了，我不明白为什么要重新整理，大家都知道它们在哪儿。这就是我 2003 年给他们看的那张幻灯片。

cues.en: It's called the myth of ideal organization.
cues.zh: 它叫“理想组织的迷思”。

cues.en: Game show.
cues.zh: 猜谜游戏。

cues.en: And so what I asked them was, I'm gonna show you nine features
cues.zh: 我问他们：我会给你们看 Word 里的九项功能，

cues.en: in Word. Tell me what they all have in common.
cues.zh: 告诉我它们有什么共同点。

cues.en: So getting the word count,
cues.zh: 查看字数，

cues.en: turning on speech and controlling that, creating a SharePoint document workspace,
cues.zh: 启用语音并进行控制，创建 SharePoint 文档工作区，

cues.en: printing envelopes,
cues.zh: 打印信封，

cues.en: opening the visual basic editor, new coding, turning on hyphenation,
cues.zh: 打开 Visual Basic 编辑器、编写新代码、启用断字，

cues.en: merging documents together, starting web conferencing,
cues.zh: 合并文档，开始网络会议，

cues.en: tweaking auto correct and IntelliSense settings. But what do all these things have in common? Does anyone wanna guess?
cues.zh: 调整自动更正和 IntelliSense 设置。这些功能有什么共同点？有人想猜猜吗？

cues.en: They're all on the Word 2,003 tools menu.
cues.zh: 它们全都在 Word 2003 的“工具”菜单里。

cues.en: So much for ideal organization.
cues.zh: 所谓的理想组织方式也就到此为止了。

cues.en: What do those things have in common? Pretty much only that they're on the tools menu.
cues.zh: 这些功能有什么共同点？差不多就只是它们都在“工具”菜单里而已。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the the thing that we used instead of index cards
cues.zh: 我们用来替代索引卡片的工具

cues.en: to find out where... How people thought things should be organized was a tool that we called SortIt. And every time people would come into the usability lab
cues.zh: 用来了解大家认为东西应该怎么组织的，是一个叫 SortIt 的工具。多年来，每次有人来到可用性实验室，

cues.en: for years, the first thing we'd have them do is use this tool called SortIt. And SortIt is a is a web tool that has a bunch of commands on the left side.
cues.zh: 我们让他们做的第一件事就是使用这个叫 SortIt 的工具。SortIt 是一个 Web 工具，左侧列了一堆命令。

cues.en: So these are all the commands in in Word, and you go through them one one by one. It would tell you what the command does, like background, change the background color. And then here's a possible organization. In this case, we were testing the Word 2,003 menus.
cues.zh: 这些就是 Word 里的所有命令，你可以逐个查看。它会告诉你命令的作用，比如“背景”可以更改背景颜色。这里还有一种可能的组织方式。当时我们在测试 Word 2003 的菜单。

cues.en: And then it would create an organization as you go. So this was designed when we were doing the Word 2,003 menus just to see how well were people able to predict the existing menu structure. Like, how well did people really know the menu structure? As we went as we went on, we introduced
cues.zh: 之后，它会随着你的操作逐步整理出一种组织方式。我们设计这个实验，是为了测试 Word 2003 的菜单，看看人们能不能预测现有的菜单结构。也就是说，人们到底有多熟悉菜单结构？随着实验进行，我们又加入了

cues.en: additional,
cues.zh: 其他的，

cues.en: you know, additional organizations like here's one set of tabs, which things work and which things don't. Turns out that most things have pretty good affinity. There are a few commands that were problematic the entire way through.
cues.zh: 你知道，又加入了其他组织方式，比如这一组标签页，看看哪些项目能用，哪些不能。结果发现，大多数项目的归类都挺合理。但有几个命令从头到尾都很难归类。

cues.en: Headers and footers.
cues.zh: 页眉和页脚。

cues.en: 50% of people believe it's an insert thing, and 50% of people tend to think it's a property of the page.
cues.zh: 一半的人认为它属于“插入”操作，另一半人则倾向于认为它是页面属性。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you could duplicate it in both places, that creates confusion because it's like I know this thing used to be on the tab next to
cues.zh: 你可以把它同时放在两处，但这又会造成混乱，比如用户会想：我记得这东西以前就在页眉旁边的标签页里，

cues.en: header and now it's not there. So there are a couple of tough ones where you just had to make choices.
cues.zh: 结果现在找不到了。所以确实有一些棘手的情况，你只能做取舍。

cues.en: But overall,
cues.zh: 但总体而言，

cues.en: could learn some pretty interesting things.
cues.zh: 我们还是能从中发现一些很有意思的事情。

cues.en: Another super interesting thing for us was eye tracking.
cues.zh: 另一件让我们特别感兴趣的事是眼动追踪。

cues.en: So this isn't actually like you strap on a huge helmet or anything. It actually turns out if you come into our usability labs, our monitors can watch you. I don't know how that works, think it involves a lot of expense.
cues.zh: 所以这其实不是要你戴上一顶巨大的头盔之类的。事实证明，只要你走进我们的可用性实验室，显示器就能观察你。我也不知道这是怎么做到的，感觉要花不少钱。

cues.en: But just
cues.zh: 不过就是

cues.en: sitting there, it's like watching your retinas.
cues.zh: 坐在那里，它就像在观察你的视网膜。

cues.en: And it's actually very interesting, because where people look is oftentimes more interesting than where their mouse cursor goes. It helps us to understand,
cues.zh: 这其实很有意思，因为人们看哪里，往往比鼠标光标移动到哪里更有意思。这能帮助我们了解：

cues.en: do Japanese users look at things different than American users, right to left languages? There are two kinds of eye tracking we did. So heat map is designed to show overall on the UI where do people look the most.
cues.zh: 日本用户看东西的方式是否和美国用户不同？从右向左书写的语言又有什么特点？我们做了两种眼动追踪。其中一种是热力图，用来展示人们在用户界面上最常看哪里。

cues.en: So it's sort of hot where people look the most, and you can see the little green spots where they haven't looked much.
cues.zh: 大家看最多的地方颜色就偏暖，而那些没怎么看的地方，就能看到一些绿色小点。

cues.en: Then gaze tracking,
cues.zh: 然后是视线追踪，

cues.en: which is sort of a blue line that shoots around and you get bigger circles when someone stops in one place for a while, like this one here that you see. And then it shows you directionally, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. This was someone that was looking at for the bold button, and doing quite well at it.
cues.zh: 就是这种到处穿梭的蓝线，当视线在某个地方停留较久时，圆圈就会变大，就像大家在这里看到的一样。接着它会按方向标出 1、2、3、4、5、6、7、8。这是有人在找“加粗”按钮，而且找得挺顺利的。

cues.en: Suffice to say, people don't always do
cues.zh: 总之，人们的眼动追踪表现

cues.en: that well at the eye tracking.
cues.zh: 并不总是那么好。

cues.en: So you can learn a lot from eye tracking. And just for posterity, here's a here's a similar one from an office 2007
cues.zh: 眼动追踪能告诉你很多东西。留个记录，这里还有一个类似的案例，来自我们对 Office 2007 的一项

cues.en: study that we did.
cues.zh: 研究。

cues.en: Yay. So we feel good about that.
cues.zh: 太好了，我们对此很满意。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the reason that you do all this evaluation is so that you can do one thing. And this is the most important word in the Office 2007,
cues.zh: 你做所有这些评估，目的就是做到一件事。这是 Office 2007

cues.en: design vocabulary.
cues.zh: 设计流程中最重要的一个词。

cues.en: This iteration.
cues.zh: 迭代。

cues.en: We knew that we would have to continually
cues.zh: 我们知道，必须不断

cues.en: beat the drum. That we'd continually have to revise the product again and again and again as we evaluate it. So there's no point evaluating something if you're not gonna do something about it. So iteration was super important. And this is how we built it into the product cycle.
cues.zh: 强调这一点。评估之后，我们得一遍又一遍地修改产品。所以，如果评估之后什么都不做，那评估也就没有意义。迭代至关重要，这就是我们把它融入产品开发周期的方式。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: for us it's about you design something, you prototype something, and you evaluate something.
cues.zh: 对我们来说，流程就是：做设计、做原型，然后做评估。

cues.en: Ideally,
cues.zh: 理想情况下，

cues.en: you can take that green arrow back up to design
cues.zh: 你可以沿着那条绿色箭头直接回到设计阶段，

cues.en: and just go around and around and around with that because that's cheaper. But we also knew that we'd have to do the big circle, which is sometimes we would code things and then reevaluate them and have to be willing to go back to the design phase with it. Which is to say if you can't do the short circle,
cues.zh: 然后就这样一圈又一圈地快速迭代，因为这样成本更低。但我们也清楚必须走大循环，也就是有时把代码写出来，再重新评估，并愿意因此推倒重回设计阶段。换句话说，如果你不能走这个短循环——

cues.en: if you can only do the short circle, then you'll miss a bunch of opportunities to fix things once people have the actual product. So we did both of those. And what that required was planning time for iteration into the dev schedule. We knew certain things we'd have to do three times to get right.
cues.zh: 或者说如果你只走短循环，那一旦用户拿到真正的产品，你就会错失大量修补问题的机会。所以这两种循环我们都走了。这就要求我们在开发排期中，必须预留出迭代的时间。我们很清楚，有些东西可能得做上三遍才能真正做好。

cues.en: Microsoft has this history of getting it right the third time. And so we figured we better do it three times during the product cycle for some things in order to get them right. So we designed an architecture that made it possible for us to make changes late in the cycle. We told people from the beginning, hey, we're going to be making a bunch of changes six months before we ship. What would it take to build an architecture that would make that less scary?
cues.zh: 微软有个传统，事情通常要到第三次才能做对。所以我们觉得，有些事情在产品周期里最好做上三遍，才能做到位。于是我们设计了一套架构，让我们能在周期后期做出调整。从一开始我们就告诉大家：“嘿，产品发布前六个月，我们会做一大堆改动。”要打造怎样的架构，才能让这件事没那么吓人？

cues.en: So here's a case study of some place where we iterated and iterated and iterated to try to get something right.
cues.zh: 这里有个案例，我们在上面反复迭代，只为了把它做好。

cues.en: So this is around object formatting, which is like when you insert a picture into the document,
cues.zh: 这是关于对象格式化的，比如你在文档里插入一张图片，

cues.en: how do you format it?
cues.zh: 你要怎么给它调格式？

cues.en: So our first thought was, we'll just have a format tab.
cues.zh: 我们最初的想法是，直接加一个“格式”选项卡。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: that seems to make sense. We'll just put all of the
cues.zh: 这看似挺合理的。我们把所有对象格式化所需的

cues.en: UI you need to format all of the objects inside the format tab. So when you have a picture selected, you have all the picture stuff in here. Well there are two problems with that. One is the format tab was constantly changing. So when you had a picture or a table up, it had different things in it and people were very confused by that. Also,
cues.zh: UI 全塞进这个“格式”选项卡里。选中图片时，相关的图片工具就都在这里。但这存在两个问题：一是这个“格式”选项卡老在变。选中图片或表格时，里面的内容完全不同，这让用户非常困惑。另外，

cues.en: there's a heck of a lot of formatting stuff in Office and it didn't fit into one tab at all. Even when you just
cues.zh: Office 里的格式化功能实在太多了，一个选项卡根本装不下。哪怕你只

cues.en: piled everything into big buttons. So we ended up with format one, format two, and format three, trying to come up with different names for them. But it it just was clear that that wasn't gonna work. And it also violated our design tenant of contextualization.
cues.zh: 我们把所有东西都塞进了大按钮里，最后就有了格式一、格式二、格式三，还得想办法给它们取不同的名字。但很明显，这行不通，也违背了我们设计原则中的情境化要求。

cues.en: So our next thought was on object commands, which is, okay, get rid of the formatting tab altogether. Formatting stuff doesn't live in the ribbon anymore. Where it actually lives is down by the object. So when I click the picture, it will bring up all the UI for formatting it right around it. And then I can click these little buttons and I can get to different things right next to the right next to the picture.
cues.zh: 接下来我们想到了对象命令：干脆彻底去掉格式选项卡。格式工具不再放在功能区里，而是放到对象旁边。点击图片时，所有图片格式设置都会显示在图片周围。我可以点击这些小按钮，在图片旁边找到不同的选项。

cues.en: This violated everything, right? It's like now there's another place for commands.
cues.zh: 这完全违背了一切原则，对吧？就好像现在又多了一个放命令的地方。

cues.en: Some of the stuff's in the ribbon, some isn't. It also only works when you don't have any text here and the picture's small and bunch of reasons that this this didn't work.
cues.zh: 有些东西在功能区（Ribbon）里，有些又不在。而且它只在没有文本、图片又很小的时候才管用，总之有太多理由说明这行不通。

cues.en: So our next thought was something called immersive experiences.
cues.zh: 所以我们接下来的想法是一种叫做“沉浸式体验”的东西。

cues.en: So here's the idea behind immersive experiences. Here's a picture of Abraham Lincoln. And if you notice, there's no format tab up here. And when I click this picture,
cues.zh: 沉浸式体验的核心思路是这样的。这里有一张 Abraham Lincoln 的照片。大家注意看，上面并没有格式选项卡。而当我点击这张图片时，

cues.en: we bring up a little thing that says show picture tools. If I click that, the entire app changes to now become the picture app.
cues.zh: 我们弹出了一个小提示，写着“显示图片工具”。如果我点击它，整个应用就会完全切换成一个图片应用。

cues.en: So the normal tabs are gone and a new ribbon shows up for a picture. It's your picture tools. cues.en: document to a guy that has Office 2,003,
cues.zh: 文档发给一个用 Office 2003 的人，

cues.en: I'm very unfriendly to you, but I like Office 2,007, but I cannot understand why you have done this, I would say, unfriendly
cues.zh: 我对你不太友好，但我喜欢 Office 2007，只是不明白你们为什么这么做，我得说，这种

cues.zh: 方式很不友好，

cues.zh: 让所有文档都无法兼容 Mac 和其他 PC 版本的 Office。所以……他指的是 Office 2007 更改了文件格式，

cues.zh: 这是出于需要一种基于开放标准的新文件格式，

cues.zh: 基于 XML，这是很多客户想要的。所以这就是 Office 2007 的默认文件格式。

cues.zh: 我们所做的是，

cues.en: And that's also true of the Mac versions of it. But if someone has not, if they just have the CD and has it installed, and hasn't updated, they don't have any of the security updates or anything, then they won't be able to to recognize it.
cues.zh: Mac 版本也是如此。但如果有人没更新，只是用光盘装了软件，没有任何安全更新之类的补丁，那就无法识别这些格式。

cues.en: So our hope is that people
cues.zh: 所以我们希望大家

cues.en: update to the most recent service pack of those apps, or in organizations where they have lots of old versions and aren't willing to update them that they use the old file formats.
cues.zh: 把这些应用更新到最新的服务包；对于有很多旧版本、又不愿更新的组织，则使用旧文件格式。

cues.zh: 我不是文件格式变更方面的专家，但据我了解，他们大致是这样推进的。不过，确实有必要采用更现代的文件格式，它基于 XML，

cues.en: because a lot of world governments
cues.zh: 因为世界上很多国家的政府

cues.zh: 包括欧盟在内的许多地方都决定，不会存储任何非 XML 开放文件格式的信息。所以有必要从旧的二进制文件格式改为新格式。

cues.zh: 但我建议你朋友装个 Office 2003 的补丁包

cues.zh: 有的。关于功能区是否适用，我会考虑这么几点。

cues.en: So one of them is that there's a trade off with screen real estate, which is to say if you can get by with
cues.zh: 其一就是屏幕空间的取舍，也就是说如果你完全够用，

cues.en: you only have 15 commands in your product,
cues.zh: 产品里总共就 15 个命令，

cues.en: then
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: I don't know if it's warranted to... Like if if all you're gonna do is just take a toolbar that you have and make them bigger toolbar buttons, I don't think you're actually
cues.zh: 我觉得就没必要……比如如果你只是把现有的工具栏拿过来，把按钮做大一点，我觉得你其实

cues.zh: 第三种做法是，如果你愿意从结果导向设计的角度重新思考产品。一旦你想开始构建一些库，

cues.zh: 构建一些功能的可视化呈现，

cues.zh: 那你就需要功能区那样的空间

cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.zh: 从文档编辑到流程导向的应用，

cues.zh: 再到工具和实用程序。我不认为真有哪种应用天然适合。我觉得更多取决于它有多少功能，以及你是否愿意彻底转变。因为如果你只是把菜单和工具栏

cues.zh: 我们还做了另一件事，就是把很多用户界面

cues.zh: 从各处，不只是Office里的菜单和工具栏，都移到了功能区里，从而收回了一些屏幕空间。所以实际上净效果

cues.en: from 2,003 to 2007, you don't use usable... You don't lose usable screen real estate. They've kept maybe a toolbar under the ribbon, plus some panes and some other stuff, and they end up with a UI that's even more cluttered than the previous one. So I think it also needs to superset
cues.zh: 从2003到2007，你不会失去可用的屏幕空间。我看到一些合作伙伴在他们的应用里用了功能区，但有个问题，他们没这么做。他们可能在功能区下面还保留着工具栏，再加上一些窗格和其他东西，结果界面比之前还乱。所以我觉得它也需要成为

cues.en: the previous thing that you have. You have to be willing to take some things out to put a new thing in.
cues.zh: 原有界面的超集。你得愿意去掉一些东西，才能加入新东西。

cues.zh: 但这方面
